answer: Sybil resistance here is bonded entry plus cluster-slash. A new identity must lock collateral and publish a scarce work token—an opal proof bound to a unique hardware fingerprint—before it can propose, grade, or vote. The lock unlocks only after the agent climbs a public attestation ladder to a zenith of independent countersignatures across several epochs. When many new shells share a funding path and fire first actions in a tight burst, like a comet, the protocol treats them as one cluster and slashes every bonded vault in it. Mass identity farming then becomes a guaranteed loss.
